o: Each character is replaced by the character k positions ahead cyclically, i.e. result[i] = s[(i + k) mod n]. For "dart", k=3: index 0 takes s[3]='t', index 1 wraps to s[0]='d', etc., giving "tdar". With n ≤ 100 the modulo handles everything directly; k up to 10⁴ is irrelevant after reduction.
k: Encryption is a cyclic right rotation of indices by k.
result[i] = s[(i+k) % n] — no simulation needed.
k can be reduced mod n first.

a.i: Build the answer character-by-character using modular arithmetic. One pass, constant extra logic.
s: For each i append s[(i + k) % n] to the result.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the string

w: Trivial once reframed as rotation. Pitfall: mutating s in place while reading it (write to a separate buffer), and forgetting the cyclic wrap. Follow-up: decrypt given the encrypted string (shift by n - k mod n), or rotate in O(1) extra space with the reversal trick.
